cohort: 282 women with a term breech presentation who underwent an attempted ECV between January 2014 and December 2018
finding: Fetomaternal hemorrhage after ECV is rare, and even when significant, it does not appear to be associated with negative fetal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study examined fetomaternal hemorrhage after external cephalic version and found that in two cases, obstetrical management was modified due to persistent FMH, leading to one planned cesarean section and one labor induction.
